column1: # What a task moved between two preempt_off regions finds in each per_cpu field.
# scripts/check_per_cpu_carried_fields.py compares the function columns with the source;
# the verdict and the reason are a review. A refused row means: read the new use, then update it.

column8: reason

mirror of this CPU's GIC priority mask, raised and read in one region. A task holds a save's flags only while masked, so no tick can move it; an IRQ is taken only at 0, so a switched El1 frame was at 0; an El0 return resets it; irq_pmr_masked_here (#638 stage 8) is the scenario's check after its cross-CPU take, and a move after it can only switch at the window's spin, which the check is not in

the mask this CPU's running handler interrupted (#638 stage 9): written and read with IRQs masked in the same handler, before any switch it chooses, so no tick moves the reader off the CPU that wrote it; a nested stop writes 1, which only refuses
which frame this CPU's EL1 tick chose (#638 stage 8): set by the tick and taken by the same entry's after_switch, both inside one IRQ with IRQs masked, so no task moves between them
this CPU's GIC interface is configured: set once per CPU at boot, before that CPU runs a process

A process moved between the read and the use resumes with its own root installed, so address_space_release_root gets the same answer on either CPU; the two boot probes that save and restore it are boot-phase and go with the flip's fixture review

the running task's activity: the stack handoff saves it in the outgoing record (parked_activity) and loads the incoming one's with kernel_activity_set, so a task moved between an enter and its leave restores its own previous value on the new CPU; kernel_activity_of reads other CPUs only through stopped_read with the world stopped (#1159); diagnostic only

whether this CPU's tick switched the real window's opener and no El1 resume ran here since (#638 stage 9): set by the tick inside its IRQ and read and cleared by the El1 resume in kernel_process_stack_switch_complete, both with IRQs masked, so no task moves inside either region; a stale mark only hides a move from the count

logical current on this CPU, changed with its guarded trace PID/live publication; task code copies the live/handle pair in one region through kernel_process_current_read, and the witness-change effect invalidates old current authority; own exception snapshots use the approved masked-entry authority
presence of this CPU's logical current, including the live PID-zero boot thread; paired with current_handle in one authority region or owning-CPU stop capture, not inferred from a PID sentinel

the child this CPU must reap after leaving its physical stack; the hook copies handle, parent and live together then clears the flag in one region before any may_block reap, so migration during teardown uses the copied work rather than another CPU's slot
the one pending deferred reap for this CPU's stack handoff; tested and set under the run hold and copied/cleared before the hook leaves its authority region for a potentially blocking reap
paired with this CPU's deferred child and live flag; all are copied and cleared in one region before teardown, and the running task handle is refreshed after a reap that can change context

written in the exit tail's PreemptOff span and read by child_exec_reap before clone_parent_return resumes that span; the new short lexical regions do not extend across the exception return, so the reader remains on the writer CPU (#633, #638)

the deferred request for this CPU's current scheduling point; IRQ/span readers clear it before selection, boot reset closes it before teardown, and stopped DDB reads use MachineStopped rather than ordinary task authority

the scheduling gate of this CPU, not a task operation; IRQ/span paths group their decision with the own-CPU access, boot reset closes it before teardown, and DDB reads it only with MachineStopped; the EL1 count consult itself stays outside the added authority region

the physical process stack remains outgoing until the generated post-switch hook installs the incoming handle; reads and writes are in IRQ/span/short authority regions, while stop capture copies scalar identity before acknowledgement and logging compares owner words only

whether this CPU physically occupies the retained stack handle; cleared with stack-owner release and set by the incoming-stack hook, under the run guard, with no authority region spanning a stack reset or a may_block reap

set after the owning CPU's scalar stop copy and cleared after peer pen release or the inspecting CPU's final command; canonical caller gates bind publication/retirement to those phases, and a complete-stop reader cannot race a peer writer

only the owning CPU's canonical stop entry captures slot/generation/live scalar words before acknowledgement (or the inspecting CPU captures under Complete stop); readers hold MachineStopped, reject an unheld capture and revalidate the pool generation, and no opaque handle or loan escapes the stop
